name: dsa-playback
displayName: DSA Playback — Algorithm Visualizer & Big-O Explainer
description: Watch your C#, Python, C++, Rust or Java solution run step by step — pointers sliding, lists rewiring, trees filling — and see in plain words why it is O(n²). Runs on your machine, no sign-in. Built for learning data structures and algorithms.

editor/title.when: resourceLangId == csharp || resourceLangId == python || resourceLangId == cpp || resourceLangId == rust || resourceLangId == java

commandPalette.when: editorLangId == csharp || editorLangId == python || editorLangId == cpp || editorLangId == rust || editorLangId == java
editorLangId == csharp || editorLangId == python || editorLangId == cpp || editorLangId == rust || editorLangId == java

dsaPlayback.enginePath.markdownDescription: Only for development: a different `DsaViz.Engine` executable to use. Leave empty — the extension uses the engine bundled inside it.

dsaPlayback.sizes.markdownDescription: Input sizes to measure. Leave empty to let the engine choose: it starts at `10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000` and drops to small sizes on its own when an algorithm is too expensive for them — which is the only way an exponential solution gets a curve at all.

dsaPlayback.timeoutSeconds.description: Longest a whole measurement may take before the engine is stopped. This is what guarantees the editor never waits forever.

dsaPlayback.budget.description: Maximum statements a single run may execute before it is stopped. This is what keeps a runaway loop from hanging the editor.

dsaPlayback.pythonPath.markdownDescription: The Python interpreter for Python files. Leave empty to use the one selected in the Python extension, or else `python3` on your path. Needs Python 3.9 or later.

dsaPlayback.cppCompiler.markdownDescription: The C++ compiler for C++ files: a path to `clang++` or `g++`. Leave empty to use `clang++`, or else `g++`, on your path. Needs C++17.

dsaPlayback.rustc.markdownDescription: The Rust compiler for Rust files: a path to `rustc`. Leave empty to use `rustc` on your path, or rustup's in `~/.cargo/bin`.

dsaPlayback.javaHome.markdownDescription: The JDK for Java files: its folder (the one with `bin/javac`). Leave empty to use `JAVA_HOME`, or else `javac` on your path. Needs JDK 17 or later.

dsaPlayback.explainWithAI.markdownDescription: Adds an **Explain this step** button to the run view. **Turning this on sends your code to GitHub Copilot**: pressing the button sends the code you are stepping through, the current line and the variables at that step to your own Copilot, through VS Code's language-model API. Nothing is sent until you press it, and VS Code asks your permission the first time. Needs VS Code 1.90 or later and a GitHub Copilot sign-in.

steps.title: Watch two pointers move
steps.description:
Open a two-pointer solution, then press **▶ Visualize** above `TwoSum`.
[Open Two Sum II in C#](command:dsaPlayback.openSample?%5B%22TwoSumSorted.cs%22%5D) · [in Python](command:dsaPlayback.openSample?%5B%22two_sum_sorted.py%22%5D) · [in C++](command:dsaPlayback.openSample?%5B%22two_sum_sorted.cpp%22%5D) · [in Rust](command:dsaPlayback.openSample?%5B%22two_sum_sorted.rs%22%5D) · [in Java](command:dsaPlayback.openSample?%5B%22TwoSumSorted.java%22%5D)

steps.title: Try your own input on a tree
steps.description:
Open a breadth-first search, press **▶ Visualize**, then type a different tree in the box.
